texts: In this type A dissection the right axillary and the innominate arteries are both dissected, so the best choice is femoral cannulation, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest and retrograde cerebral perfusion.
The usual first choice, right axillary cannulation, is ruled out because the axillary artery is dissected and the innominate arises from the false lumen.
The femoral artery is quick to reach in a patient with tamponade and gives arterial inflow for bypass.
Retrograde cerebral perfusion through the superior vena cava protects the brain during the arrest without cannulating dissected head vessels.
Central cannulation of a leaking dissected aorta with tamponade is dangerous, and left axillary perfusion would not reliably reach the brain through an innominate fed by the false lumen.
In the picture, Chopper pushes the cannon in beside the thigh bone, and cold water flows backwards down the chimney to the lantern inside the ice.
Memory hook: when the armpit is torn, go in through the thigh and down the chimney.
